Repository Guidelines

Source: AGENTS.md

This file and CLAUDE.md must contain identical content. They are kept as twin files so any tool looking for either name finds the same guidance. When you edit one, mirror the change to the other in the same commit.

Project Overview

neurothresh is an R package for neuroimaging statistical thresholding that implements:

  1. LR-MFT (Likelihood-Ratio Matched-Filter Thresholding) with hierarchical stepdown inference — a prior-weighted soft evidence aggregation method that is provably more powerful than RFT peak-height for multi-focal/distributed brain activations.
  2. Standard baseline methods: RFT peak/cluster FWER, TFCE, cluster-FDR.

The package integrates with neuroim2 (volumetric brain imaging data structures) and neuroatlas (brain parcellations).

Project Structure & Module Organization

Core R code lives in R/, with public APIs and helpers split by method: hier_scan.R, octree_scan*.R, stepdown.R, permutation.R, rft.R, tfce.R, and cluster_fdr.R. Performance-critical Rcpp code is in src/; after changing exported C++ routines, regenerate R/RcppExports.R and src/RcppExports.cpp. Tests are in tests/testthat/, vignettes in vignettes/, benchmarks and simulation harnesses in inst/bench/, and design/API notes in specs/ plus older material in docs_old/.

Build, Test, and Development Commands

  • Rscript -e "devtools::install_deps()": install package dependencies.
  • Rscript -e "devtools::load_all()": load the package for interactive development.
  • Rscript -e "devtools::document()": regenerate roxygen docs, NAMESPACE, and .Rd files.
  • Rscript -e "Rcpp::compileAttributes()": refresh Rcpp exports after editing src/*.cpp.
  • Rscript -e "devtools::test()": run the full testthat suite.
  • Rscript -e "testthat::test_file('tests/testthat/test-permutation-core.R')": run one focused test file.
  • R CMD INSTALL .: compile and install locally.
  • R CMD check --as-cran .: run the full package check before release-oriented changes.

Architecture

Core Algorithm Flow

  1. Canonicalize input (Z/t/log10p → standardized Z-equivalent field).
  2. Build parcel roots from atlas labels with prior mass caching.
  3. Score parcels using prior-weighted statistics:
    • κ=0: Variance-stabilized diffuse score U_0(R) = Σπ(v)Z(v) / √Σπ(v)²
    • κ>0: Soft-max score S_κ(R) = (1/κ)·log(Σπ(v)exp(κZ(v)) / Σπ(v))
    • Combined: T(R) = max(U_0, max_κ S_κ)
  4. Westfall-Young step-down at parcel level for FWER control.
  5. Recursive octree descent into significant parcels with α-spending.
  6. One-pass sibling scoring (Rcpp) for children at each split.

Key Statistics

Statistic Formula Use Case
U_0(R) Σπ(v)Z(v) / √Σπ(v)² Distributed/diffuse signals
S_κ(R) (1/κ)·log(Σπ(v)·exp(κZ(v)) / Σπ(v)) Focal signals (κ large → max)
T(R) max(U_0, max_κ S_κ) Omnibus score for any pattern

Rcpp C++ Functions

Three critical Rcpp exports for performance:

  • octree_split_info_cpp() — Build child assignment and cache π/π² constants.
  • score_children_onepass_cpp() — Score all ≤8 children in single pass (streaming log-sum-exp).
  • split_indices_bbox_mass_cpp() — Split indices + compute bboxes + π masses in one pass.

Algorithm Design Notes

Why LR-MFT Beats RFT Peak-Height

RFT peak-height is a hard-max detector optimal for “one dominant peak.” LR-MFT’s soft evidence aggregation is NP-optimal for multi-focal alternatives (multiple activation blobs), which is biologically realistic for task fMRI.

Variance Stabilization (U_0)

Without scaling, singleton voxels have unit variance while large regions have tiny variance under the null. The √n_eff scaling (n_eff = Π(R)²/Π_2(R)) ensures fair comparison across scales.

Hierarchical α-Spending

Budget allocation: α_child = (α_node - α_test) · w_child where w_child ∝ π(child). This gives a clean FWER proof via union bound + nesting.

Computational Optimization

The one-pass sibling scoring eliminates O(m) vector allocations per permutation by streaming through parent voxels and updating ≤8 child accumulators simultaneously. This is the key to making permutation-based inference tractable.

Coding Style & Naming Conventions

Use two-space indentation in R, snake_case for functions and variables, and S3 method names such as print.neurothresh_result. Keep roxygen2 documentation close to exported functions and use markdown-enabled roxygen syntax. In C++, follow the existing Rcpp style: compact exported functions, explicit input validation with Rcpp::stop(), and 0-based internals with comments where R-facing indices are converted.

Testing Guidelines

Tests use testthat edition 3. Name files test-<topic>.R, and prefer small deterministic examples with fixed seeds for permutation or resampling behavior. For numerical algorithms, include invariants, edge cases, and differential checks against simpler implementations when available. Run focused tests while iterating, then devtools::test() before handoff; use R CMD check --as-cran . for broader validation.

Commit & Pull Request Guidelines

Recent commits use short imperative subjects, for example Add optional future-based parallelism to hier_scan and Improve vignette exposition for end users. Keep commits scoped by concern: code, docs, generated roxygen output, and benchmarks should be easy to review. Pull requests should summarize the statistical or API behavior changed, list validation commands run, link issues when applicable, and include plot or vignette screenshots only when visual output changes.

Agent-Specific Instructions

Do not overwrite unrelated local edits. Generated files such as NAMESPACE, man/*.Rd, and Rcpp export files should be updated only when the source change requires them. Avoid committing local artifacts like .Rcheck, .rcmdcheck_result.rds, .covr_result.rds, or benchmark outputs.

AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md must stay in sync — they are twin files with byte-identical content. Whenever you edit one, copy the same change into the other in the same commit. CI/review should reject diffs where only one of the two has been updated.
